allow_large: A version bump touches the version, the pin, the install scripts, the plugin manifests, sync output and the tests that pin them
done_when: Forge's version is 1.2.10 everywhere it is recorded (the command, the repo pin, both install scripts, the README install line, the plugin and marketplace manifests, committed hooks and workflows, uv.lock), and new and upgraded clients install v1.2.10

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The allowance covers a version bump and the sync output needed for it. This branch also adds the full Simplified Technical English skill and checker under both `.claude` and `.codex`. The new instruction to apply STE to technical output changes agent behavior in this repo and contains no release-version change. That is a second kind of work outside the recorded version-only allowance.
findings.title: The recorded allowance does not cover the added writing skill

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The proof list says `test_release_version.py` proves that new and upgraded clients install v1.2.10. At this line, the test writes a client pin directly and then calls `forge sync` twice. It never runs `forge init`, `forge upgrade`, or an installation. The named installer tests cover the platform scripts, but the list names no proof for the client upgrade path. The claim that sync proves upgraded clients install v1.2.10 is therefore unsupported.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

why: Clients and this repo need v1.2.10 for the speed fixes merged since v1.2.9: tests run once, reviews run alongside tests, stops ask plain questions and wait 30 minutes, personal worker choice
